matched_segment: Huntington's disease has primarily been described as a late-onset neurodegenerative disease.

query: However, it is preceded in its premanifest period by a prolonged presymptomatic phase followed by a prodromal phase with hardly detectable and unspecific symptoms occurring far before classical Huntington's disease becomes apparent (Ross et al., 2014).
matched_segment: However, it is preceded in its premanifest period by a prolonged presymptomatic phase followed by a prodromal phase with hardly detectable and unspecific symptoms occurring far before classical Huntington's disease becomes apparent (Ross et al., 2014).

query: These symptoms include reduced impulse control, social disengagement, low conversational participation, reduction of the concentration span and decline of clearly defined cognitive domains (Stout et al., 2011; Predict-HD Investigators of the Huntington Study Group et al., 2007; Ross et al., 2014; Labuschagne et al., 2016)
matched_segment: These symptoms include reduced impulse control, social disengagement, low conversational participation, reduction of the concentration span and decline of clearly defined cognitive domains (Stout et al., 2011; Predict-HD Investigators of the Huntington Study Group et al., 2007; Ross et al., 2014; Labuschagne et al., 2016)

matched_segment: This stage reaches back more than 15–20 years before motor symptoms become visible in patients and far before protein aggregates and neurodegeneration are observed.

query: In Huntington's disease occurrence of such very early changes is supported by the observation of early deficits in premanifest Huntington's disease mutation carriers, such as loss of phosphodiesterase 10A in the occipital lobe up to 47 years prior to disease onset (summarized in Wilson et al., 2017).

query: We hypothesize that primal functional changes in the VFDO stage of premanifest Huntington's disease open up very early vulnerable windows for disease development and preventive therapy prior to neuronal loss and may also provide promising early biomarkers for therapy development (Mehler and Gokhan, 2000; Kerschbamer and Biagioli, 2015; Humbert, 2010; Cepeda et al., 2003).

query: It seems that the visual cortex is one of the first regions that are functionally affected during disease development in Huntington's disease (Labuschagne et al., 2016; Dogan et al., 2013).
matched_segment: It seems that the visual cortex is one of the first regions that are functionally affected during disease development in Huntington's disease (Labuschagne et al., 2016; Dogan et al., 2013).

query: We show that even at the early age of 10 – 15 weeks (young adults compared to humans), the entire cortical microcircuit shifts towards a more excitable state characterized by a complex change in neuronal activity pattern and hyperactive neurons.

query: We have recently shown that mRNAs carrying CAG repeats bind to a protein complex containing the ubiquitin ligase midline 1 (MID1) in a repeat size-dependent manner.

query: Through ubiquitination MID1 regulates PP2A (protein phosphatase 2A) and mTOR (mechanistic target of rapamycin) activities and the translation of associated mRNAs (Krauss et al., 2013; Griesche et al., 2016).

query: We show here that the type II diabetes drug metformin interferes with the MID1/PP2A/mTOR protein complex and significantly reduces the translation rate of Htt mRNA, resulting in a reduction of aberrant Htt protein production in vitro and in vivo in the Hdh150 mouse model.
